We present SafeJIT, a small JavaScript engine with a speculating baseline JIT, together with a machine-checked proof in Lean 4 that its statically linked RISC-V and x86-64 executables never crash, on any input, in a model of a Linux user process. Its targets have traditionally been functional languages (Standard ML, OCaml, Haskell, and Scala), recently joined by Go. Python, which is becoming the dominant language of scientific computing, data science, and education, has remained out of reach. In this work, we close this gap with a Python backend…

An alternative, proposed in the context of path abstraction in probabilistic counterexample refinement, is to view them as a transition kernel on the free monoid on the state space, mapping paths directly to path probabilities. In this paper, we first extend the free monoid view and path abstraction algorithm to cumulative rewards on Markov reward models. items.summary: Formalises Markov chains and reward models in Isabelle/HOL using a free monoid view for path abstraction and cumulative rewards.

Category theory provides the most promising path toward reusable programming language semantics. Universal properties capture the type connectives---products, functions, sums---together with their $β$/$η$ laws. Free categorical structures identify syntactic calculi…

items.title: Partial Borrows in Rust
items.source_text: Rust ensures memory safety by requiring exclusive access to mutably borrowed data. However, a borrow can prevent access to more data than necessary. For example, a method with an &mut self parameter borrows the entire struct, even when the method uses only some of its fields. Calling the method can therefore conflict with an existing borrow of a field the method never uses, causing Rust to reject the program. Resolving such conflicts can require programmers to compromise useful abstractions, make non-local changes to their programs, or worse, resort to unsafe code. We introduce view types, a…
items.summary: Introduces view types for Rust to allow partial borrows, so methods can borrow only the fields they use, reducing borrow conflicts.
